macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall as weak data and higher Treasury yields pressure risk assets
items.summary: U.S. stocks ended lower in Monday trading, with the S&P 500 down 0.61% and the Dow off 0.21%, as investors reacted to softer economic data and rising long-term yields. The 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.3103%, its highest level since 2007, reinforcing concerns about tighter financial conditions.

items.title: Market pricing for a near-term Fed move eases after softer U.S. data
items.summary: Traders reduced expectations for an imminent Federal Reserve rate move after weak retail sales and job data, with odds of a September move falling to about 35% from roughly 55% a week earlier. The shift reflects growing confidence that the Fed may hold rates steady longer as data soften.

items.title: Dollar weakens as investors trim rate-hike bets and monitor Middle East risks
items.summary: The U.S. dollar held near multi-month lows against major currencies on Tuesday as traders scaled back expectations for near-term U.S. monetary tightening. Sentiment remained fragile amid concern that escalating Middle East tensions could further unsettle markets.

items.title: Global markets remain under pressure from bond sell-off and rising borrowing costs
items.summary: Investors are contending with a broad global bond market sell-off driven by concerns about inflation and large government deficits, which is pushing up borrowing costs. The move is adding pressure on equities and complicating the policy outlook for central banks.

items.title: Rising oil prices support some markets as geopolitical tensions keep risk appetite subdued
items.summary: Oil has been one of the main market drivers, with Brent moving back above $91 and helping energy-related shares outperform even as broader equity sentiment stays risk-off. The move reflects ongoing concern about Middle East tensions and the lack of progress on a peace deal.

items.title: U.S. market snapshot shows broad weakness ahead of the close
items.summary: U.S. equities were lower in late trading, with the S&P 500 down 0.61% and the Dow down 0.21%, reflecting continued pressure from yields and cautious sentiment. The data point to a soft risk tone across major indexes.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $64,000 as macro pressures offset recent gains
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $64,000 after rising from about $62,600 the prior day, with higher yields and weaker equities cited as headwinds. Several market trackers also showed BTC up roughly 1%–2.5% over the past 24 hours, while ETH was slightly higher or flat around $1,899–$1,906.

items.title: Crypto market rebounds broadly, with total market cap near $2.28 trillion
items.summary: Broader crypto markets climbed about 2.6% in the past 24 hours to roughly $2.28 trillion, with Bitcoin strengthening and some altcoins outperforming. Reports highlighted gains in Solana, Tron, and Hyperliquid, while BNB, XRP, Dogecoin, and Cardano were mixed or slightly weaker.

items.title: Metaplanet moves 2,100 BTC to launch U.S. treasury strategy
items.summary: Metaplanet announced a major treasury move involving 2,100 BTC, extending its corporate Bitcoin accumulation strategy into the U.S. market. The development was one of the most notable project and treasury headlines in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Toyota Finance launches ¥1 billion tokenized bond via Toyota Wallet
items.summary: Toyota Finance launched a ¥1 billion tokenized bond through Toyota Wallet, underscoring continued experimentation with real-world asset tokenization. The move adds to a growing list of corporate blockchain product rollouts.

items.title: World Liberty Financial gets conditional OCC bank charter approval
items.summary: Regulatory news centered on the OCC conditionally approving a bank charter for World Liberty Financial, a notable step for a Trump-linked crypto project. The approval was highlighted alongside broader scrutiny of crypto firms and compliance issues.

items.title: Binance plans FCA application in the UK
items.summary: Binance said it plans to pursue an FCA application in the UK, signaling another effort to strengthen its regulatory standing in a major market. The announcement came amid heightened global attention on exchange compliance.

items.title: EU considers country-wide crypto bans over Russia sanctions evasion
items.summary: European regulators reportedly opened the door to country-wide crypto bans as part of efforts to curb Russia sanctions evasion. The discussion adds to ongoing pressure on crypto firms operating in Europe.

items.title: Ethereum developers warn Glamsterdam upgrade could break wallets and gas tools
items.summary: Ethereum developers warned that the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade could create compatibility issues for wallets and gas-related tooling. The warning is one of the key project-development items from the past day.

items.title: Conflux deposits and withdrawals to be temporarily suspended for network upgrade
items.summary: Crypto market news reported that Binance will temporarily suspend Conflux deposits and withdrawals during a network upgrade. The notice reflects ongoing maintenance and coordination around blockchain infrastructure changes.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum remain in focus as traders watch inflation and Fed signals
items.summary: Several outlets tied the latest crypto move to cooling inflation, falling Treasury yields, and expectations around the Fed, with Bitcoin near $64,000 and Ethereum near $1,900. Market commentary also noted sizable ETF outflows even as prices recovered.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with stronger safeguards
items.summary: OpenAI introduced a teen-focused version of ChatGPT with parental controls, study tools, and added safety measures. Coverage says the rollout is aimed at making the chatbot more age-appropriate amid growing scrutiny over youth use of AI.

items.title: OpenAI and NVIDIA reportedly back massive AI campus buildout
items.summary: Multiple AI news roundups report a major OpenAI–NVIDIA infrastructure announcement tied to an 8 GW megacampus and large-scale lease and power obligations. If confirmed, it would rank among the largest AI infrastructure commitments yet and signals continued hyperscale spending on compute.

items.title: Groq raises $350 million at a lower valuation
items.summary: Groq reportedly secured a $350 million funding round even though the company’s valuation was lower than in its prior raise. The deal still drew NVIDIA participation, underscoring investor interest in specialized AI chips and inference infrastructure.

items.title: Cursor launches Origin, a direct rival to GitHub
items.summary: AI developer-tool coverage says Cursor quietly launched Origin, an AI-native code hosting platform positioned as a competitor to GitHub. The move highlights continued product expansion in the AI coding stack.

items.title: ByteDance signs an AI copyright framework with the Motion Picture Association
items.summary: A news roundup reports that ByteDance reached what is described as Hollywood’s first formal AI copyright framework with the Motion Picture Association. The development points to a growing industry trend toward negotiated rules for AI-generated or AI-assisted content.

items.title: Cartesia releases Sonic-3.6 text-to-speech model
items.summary: AI coverage says Cartesia launched Sonic-3.6, described as a new state-of-the-art text-to-speech model with support for 44 languages. The release reflects ongoing competition in voice AI and multilingual speech generation.

items.title: Higgsfield raises $400 million in Series B
items.summary: A roundup says Higgsfield closed a $400 million Series B that pushed its valuation to $5.4 billion. The financing is another sign that capital remains concentrated in fast-growing generative AI startups.

items.title: Alibaba expands Qwen and releases open model weights
items.summary: Recent AI coverage says Alibaba released the weights for a more advanced model and expanded the Qwen family with a multimodal 27B parameter version designed for local execution and agentic tasks. That suggests continued competition among open and open-weight model ecosystems.

items.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.3 with coding and safety improvements
items.summary: Coverage reports that Z.ai released GLM-5.3, claiming gains in coding and safety without retraining the base model. The announcement adds to the recent wave of incremental model upgrades focused on reliability rather than sheer scale.

items.title: Microsoft unifies Copilot apps and cuts some AI features
items.summary: Reports say Microsoft is merging its Copilot apps while removing features such as Group Chats, podcasts, and the Mico character. The change shows a broader industry trend toward simplifying AI products and pruning experimental features.

items.title: Gemini and ChatGPT both cross major user milestones
items.summary: A news roundup says Google reported Gemini reaching 1 billion monthly users, while OpenAI said ChatGPT also surpassed 1 billion users. If accurate, the figures reinforce how consumer AI assistants have become mainstream products.

items.title: Baidu reports another revenue decline amid AI investments
items.summary: Recent financial coverage says Baidu posted its fifth straight quarterly revenue drop even as it continues to bet heavily on AI. The result underscores the pressure on large internet companies to convert AI spending into growth.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Netflix shuts down two game studios, including Night School
items.summary: Netflix is closing two of its internal game studios, including Night School Studio, the developer of Oxenfree. The move comes despite Netflix previously praising the studio’s performance.

items.title: Valve updates AI disclosure guidelines for developers
items.summary: Valve has updated its Steam AI disclosure policy, allowing developers to use AI-powered tools under clearer disclosure rules. The change affects how games using generative AI or other AI-assisted systems are labeled on Steam.

items.title: GeForce Now adds Firefox support
items.summary: Nvidia’s GeForce Now cloud gaming service now supports streaming in Mozilla Firefox, expanding browser compatibility beyond Chrome, Safari, Edge, and Opera GX.

items.title: Control Resonant goes gold, physical release delayed
items.summary: Control Resonant has gone gold, meaning development is complete, but its physical edition has been pushed back to October 15.

items.title: Ubisoft announces 'The Division' movie
items.summary: Ubisoft has announced a film adaptation of The Division with Jessica Chastain and Jake Gyllenhaal attached. The project adds another high-profile game-to-film adaptation to Ubisoft’s slate.

items.title: Sonic Frontiers crosses 5 million sales
items.summary: SEGA says Sonic Frontiers has now sold more than 5 million copies. The milestone underscores the game’s continued commercial success.

items.title: Shinji Mikami leaves Tango Gameworks
items.summary: Shinji Mikami, the creator of Resident Evil, is leaving Tango Gameworks after 12 years. The departure marks a major leadership change for the studio.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts IV launch window reportedly set for late 2027
items.summary: Square Enix has confirmed a late 2027 release window for Kingdom Hearts IV, according to the reported gaming news roundup. This provides one of the clearest timing updates yet for the long-awaited sequel.

items.title: BGMI Lite announced for India
items.summary: Krafton has announced BGMI Lite for India, with launch expected by the end of 2026. The lighter version is aimed at broadening access on lower-end devices.

items.title: Gaming industry layoffs continue in 2026
items.summary: A Chinese gaming news roundup reports that the industry has averaged 44 job losses per day so far in 2026, highlighting continued workforce pressure across the sector.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple rolls out new EU App Store business terms
items.summary: Apple announced revised business terms for apps in the European Union, including a new 5% Core Technology Commission and updated App Store commission tiers. The changes take effect October 1 and are meant to resolve disputes with the European Commission.

items.title: Fairphone launches repairable Gen. 6+ phone in the U.S.
items.summary: Dutch maker Fairphone has begun selling its repairable flagship phone in the United States for $650. The company says it plans to keep releasing new phone generations every two years.

items.title: Weave Communications to go private in $650 million deal
items.summary: Francisco Partners plans to take patient engagement software company Weave Communications private for about $650 million. Weave went public in 2021 at a valuation of roughly $1.5 billion.

items.title: Nvidia to back massive Ohio data center campus tied to OpenAI lease
items.summary: Filing details indicate Nvidia agreed to provide up to $105 billion in support for SB Energy's new Ohio data center campus that OpenAI is set to lease. Nvidia is also reported to be investing $1.5 billion in SB Energy.

items.title: Groq raises $350 million at a lower valuation
items.summary: Groq raised $350 million in fresh funding at about half its previous valuation. The company is also shifting its strategy toward a neocloud business while adding Nvidia to the round.

items.title: Lenovo India tops $2 billion in revenue
items.summary: Lenovo India surpassed $2 billion in revenue and is expanding its manufacturing footprint. The company said AI remains part of its broader growth and production strategy.

items.title: YouTube changes how it counts video views
items.summary: YouTube will now count a view as soon as a video starts playing, rather than waiting for 30 seconds of watch time. The change is expected to increase reported view counts across the platform.
